evals.name: contexto-e-conteineres-pt
evals.prompt: Preciso dos diagramas C4 (contexto e contêineres) da plataforma de agendamento "ConsultaFácil" para a proposta. Pacientes marcam consultas pelo app (React Native) e as clínicas gerenciam a agenda num painel web (Angular). Os dois falam com uma API em .NET 8 via REST, que grava no SQL Server e publica eventos de agendamento numa fila Azure Service Bus. Um worker em .NET consome a fila e envia lembretes por WhatsApp usando a API da Twilio e cobra a taxa de reserva pelo gateway da Stone. O login dos pacientes é feito pelo Azure AD B2C. Gere o HTML interativo.
evals.expected_output: One c4 model (pt-BR) with a systemContext and a container view of ConsultaFácil, delivered as two linked HTML files that validate in showcase: people Paciente and Clínica; containers app, painel, API, worker, banco (cylinder) and fila with their technologies; Twilio, Stone and Azure AD B2C as external systems; relationships with intent and protocol; the queue relationships async; acronyms explained in meta.glossary.
assertions: Output is a folder with one standalone HTML per view (context and containers) that render SVG diagrams
The context view title names the diagram type and the system (e.g. 'Diagrama de contexto do sistema ConsultaFácil')
Every container shows its technology in the box ([Contêiner: …])
Twilio, Stone and Azure AD B2C are drawn as external systems (grey) and not as containers
Relationships between containers carry a protocol (REST/HTTPS, SQL, AMQP or similar)
The worker's relationship with the queue is shown as asynchronous (dashed)
Double-clicking the system in the context view opens the container view
Validation reports 0 errors and 0 warnings in both views, or every remaining waiver has an explicit reason

evals.name: component-view-en
evals.prompt: Add a C4 component diagram for our Orders Service (Kotlin, Spring Boot) to the architecture: it has an OrdersController (Spring MVC) that calls a PricingService and an OrderRepository (Spring Data JPA, PostgreSQL), and an OutboxPublisher that pushes OrderPlaced events to Kafka. The web shop (Next.js) calls the controller over JSON/HTTPS. Produce the context, container and component views.
evals.expected_output: One c4 model with context, container and component views; components authored with parent = the Orders Service container and relationships authored between components; the container view shows the lifted relationships (web shop → Orders Service, Orders Service → database, Orders Service → Kafka) without duplicates; Kafka modelled as a container or external system with technology; the component view scoped to the Orders Service.
assertions: There are three linked HTML views: context, containers and components
The component view shows OrdersController, PricingService, OrderRepository and OutboxPublisher inside the Orders Service boundary
The container view shows Web Shop → Orders Service once, even though the relationship was authored to a component
In-process relationships between components are not forced to declare a protocol
Relationships that cross container boundaries declare a technology
The response does not invent technologies that were not given

evals.name: missing-facts-pending
evals.prompt: Draw a C4 context diagram for our HR portal. Employees and managers use it; it pulls salaries from the payroll system and sends approvals to the ERP. I don't know how it talks to payroll yet.
evals.expected_output: A c4 model with a systemContext view of the HR portal: two people, the portal, Payroll and ERP (ERP explained in meta.glossary); because only a context view is requested no protocol is required, and the unknown integration detail is reported back to the user as an open question instead of being invented.
assertions: The context view shows Employee, Manager, HR Portal, Payroll and ERP
Every relationship has an intent label (no bare 'uses')
ERP is explained in the acronyms card
The response lists the unknown payroll integration as an open question and does not invent a protocol
